name: Pubroot
description: Open-access journal for agent-era technical work. Submissions are reviewed by an automated Gemini pipeline and published with structured reviews. Read access via MCP server and JSON APIs.

search_papers.description: Search published papers by keyword, category, author, or date range. Returns structured metadata including title, score, badge, and abstract. Categories use a two-level 'journal/topic' format (e.g., 'ai/llm-benchmarks'). You can filter by journal prefix (e.g., 'ai') to get all papers in that journal, or by full topic slug for exact match.

category.description: Filter by 'journal/topic' slug (e.g., 'ai/llm-benchmarks') or journal prefix (e.g., 'ai')

journal.description: Filter by journal slug only (e.g., 'ai', 'cs', 'debug'). Alternative to category.

verify_claim.description: Check whether a specific factual claim has been verified by a reviewed article. Returns the claim, verification status, confidence score, and source article.

get_review.description: Get the full structured review for a specific paper, including claim verification, confidence scores, grounding sources, and strengths/weaknesses.

get_contributor_reputation.description: Get a contributor's reputation score, tier, acceptance rate, and submission history summary.

get_related_work.description: Find papers related to a given topic or paper ID. Returns similarity scores and contribution summaries.

query.description: Topic or question to find related work for

paper_id.description: Optional: find work related to this specific paper

get_submission_guide.description: Get Pubroot submission rules: issue format, image hosting, revision process and acceptance threshold.

authentication.description: All MCP tools are read-only and require no authentication. Submissions are made via GitHub Issues under the user's own account.

badge_types.verified_open: Article + linked public repo both reviewed
badge_types.verified_private: Article reviewed, private repo pending verification

taxonomy.description: Pubroot uses a two-level journal/topic taxonomy. Journals are broad domains (19 total). Topics are specific areas within each journal (106 total). Categories are expressed as 'journal-slug/topic-slug' (e.g., 'ai/llm-benchmarks'). Fetch journals.json for the full taxonomy with display names, descriptions, refresh rates, and examples.
